name: MySQL
shortDescription: MySQL stores data in tables, like a class list with rows and columns. Learn to add records and find answers. These lessons use a separate MySQL tool.
highlights: Make tables and add records
Find and sort the rows you need
Keep related records together

name: PostgreSQL
shortDescription: PostgreSQL stores related data in tables and provides SQL tools for asking questions. Learn a small book table, safe changes and a few PostgreSQL features such as JSONB and useful returned values.
highlights: Practise make a practice table
Practise count rows in each group
Practise use an array for a small value list

name: Microsoft SQL Server
shortDescription: SQL Server is Microsoft's table database. Its SQL form is called T-SQL. Learn named values, small tables and queries, then meet safe conversions, numbered results and transactions using sample records.
highlights: Practise keep a local variable
Practise summarise groups
Practise undo a sample transaction

name: Oracle Database
shortDescription: Oracle Database stores data in tables and includes the PL/SQL programming language. Learn clear queries, dates, row rules and a small block of PL/SQL with sample book information.
highlights: Practise choose number and text types
Practise handle a missing value
Practise read a sequence value

name: MongoDB
shortDescription: MongoDB stores data in records called documents. A document can hold a name, a score and a list. Learn to add, find and change simple records.
highlights: Make a document with named values
Find and change saved records
Group records into collections

name: Redis
shortDescription: Redis stores values under keys and offers useful data structures. It often keeps fast temporary data such as counts and queues. Learn its strings, lists and sets with clearly named practice keys.
highlights: Practise count with an atomic increment
Practise use a list as a small queue
Practise group commands with multi

name: SQLite
shortDescription: SQLite is a small SQL database that can run inside an app. This site uses SQLite for its SQL playground. Learn tables, filters, joins and safe sample changes with examples that run right in the browser.
highlights: Practise create a sample table
Practise count a group of rows
Practise undo an unfinished change

name: MariaDB
shortDescription: MariaDB is a table database with many roots shared with MySQL. This course uses its own client and features. Learn a small table, grouped text, safe updates and a practice backup in a separate database.
highlights: Practise create an innodb sample table
Practise join grouped text
Practise undo row changes in a transaction

name: Firebase Firestore
shortDescription: Firestore stores records as documents in collections. This course uses the local Firebase emulator to learn reads, changes, queries and rules with fake book data. The learning website itself does not connect to Firebase.
highlights: Practise start a local emulator
Practise change selected fields
Practise group writes in a batch

name: Supabase
shortDescription: Supabase puts useful app tools around PostgreSQL. This starter course uses a local Supabase project and a public sample book list. Learn tables, read permissions and clear client queries without adding a login to this website.
highlights: Practise create a local sample table
Practise make a local client
Practise count without requesting every row

name: Elasticsearch
shortDescription: Elasticsearch searches documents and summarises their fields. It uses indexes, mappings and JSON requests. Learn a tiny book index, the difference between search and exact filters, and clear result summaries.
highlights: Practise choose field mappings first
Practise filter an exact category
Practise count categories with an aggregation

name: Cassandra
shortDescription: Cassandra stores data across machines and groups rows by a partition key. You design a table around the question you need to ask. Learn a small reading log with CQL and see why its rules differ from ordinary table joins.
highlights: Practise design a table for one question
Practise keep partitions a manageable size
Practise group a small related write

name: Neo4j
shortDescription: Neo4j stores a graph: things are nodes, and connections are relationships. Its query language is Cypher. Learn a small graph of readers and books, then ask questions by following named connections.
highlights: Practise find a node by a property
Practise follow a relationship
Practise keep a reader with no match

name: DynamoDB
shortDescription: DynamoDB stores items addressed by keys. A partition key groups related items, and a sort key orders them within that group. Learn the request shapes with a local practice table and a small book list.
highlights: Practise create a local keyed table
Practise use a sort-key prefix
Practise understand filters and read cost
